item.title: Mbappé apologizes to Chinese people after backlash, but damage may take time to repair: observer
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27 23:03:00
Kylian Mbappé, a Real Madrid player in Spain's LaLiga French football star Kylian Mbappé apologized to the Chinese people on Tuesday after his erroneous remarks triggered widespread criticism in China, while the Chinese Football Association (CFA) said it had lodged serious representations with Real Madrid and demanded a formal public apology from the club. "My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world," Mbappé said in a statement on Tuesday. "I apologize to everyone my words have upset. This was absolutely not my intention. I have deep respect for the Chinese people and their history, and I am sincerely sorry," he added. The apology came as the controversy continued to escalate, with at least three Chinese companies - beverage maker Dongpeng, dairy giant Mengniu and cheese producer Milkground - announcing the termination of their commercial partnerships with the Real Madrid forward. The controversy also prompted China's state broadcaster CMG to suspend broadcasts of LaLiga matches, all games featuring Mbappé, and advertisements endorsing the player, CMG said. In a statement on Tuesday, the CFA said it attached great importance to the incident and had immediately lodged serious representations with Real Madrid, demanding that the player involved and the club issue formal public apologies. The association's statement puts the focus not only on the player's apology but also on the responsibility of his club, one of the most prominent teams in world football, in addressing conduct by its players that causes offence internationally. RedNote, a Chinese social media platform that had a cooperation contract with Mbappé in 2024, said Tuesday that it was reviewing and removing related content and materials. Real Madrid has not made any official statement regarding the issue as of press time on Tuesday. LaLiga also issued a statement on Tuesday expressing regret over the offence caused to Chinese fans. It said Mbappé's comments had been made in a personal capacity and did not represent the league. La Liga President Javier Tebas also apologized to Chinese fans, saying the league would work with clubs and players to strengthen cultural awareness and respect. "I take on the responsibility of working with our clubs and players to strengthen awareness of and respect for different cultures," Tebas said. Zhu Meng, a Beijing-based sports commentator, said Mbappé had responded relatively quickly to the controversy with his apology, but it remained unclear whether the apology could repair the damage caused by his remarks. "From a commercial perspective, all the brands that had partnerships with him have chosen to distance themselves. Once market trust is damaged, it is difficult to restore it quickly," Zhu told the Global Times. "Even if his performance on the pitch remains strong, it will still take time before he can regain his commercial value in the Chinese market," Zhu noted. Across Chinese social media on Tuesday, calls for Mbappé to apologize spread rapidly. Some users also called for a boycott of the footballer. Commentary in Chinese media also questioned the conduct of public figures seeking commercial opportunities in China while making remarks perceived as disrespectful to Chinese people. "The Chinese market embraces the world with open arms, welcoming celebrities, athletes, businesses and brands from all countries to share in its development opportunities," Jimu News said in a commentary.

item.title: MEPs visit China amid EU's mixed trade signals; experts warn Brussels' 'dual track' approach undermines good-faith talks
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27 22:30:00
The European Union (EU) flags in front of EU headquarters in Brussels, Belgium. Photo: VCG A 12-member delegation from the European Parliament's International Trade committee (INTA) is touring Beijing, Hangzhou and Shanghai from Tuesday to Thursday for talks with Chinese counterparts and government officials, as well as visits to Chinese tech innovators Unitree and BrainCo. It marks the committee's first China trip since 2018 and the European Parliament's fourth China delegation this year, the parliament said in a release. Yet Chinese experts warn the EU is sending mixed signals by engaging in dialogue while planning new curbs on Chinese imports, arguing such double-dealing undermines good-faith talks. Bloomberg reported that Brussels plans to use safeguard measures to cut imports of Chinese chemicals, furniture and machinery, possibly as early as the first quarter of 2027. Since July, low-value parcels entering the EU have faced a temporary customs duty of 3 euro ($3.34), and from November 1, a further handling fee of 2 euros will apply, AFP reported, noting that about 93 percent of such parcels previously came from China. Mixed signals cloud trade talks The core problem, Chinese experts said, is that the European side cannot show a gesture of seeking engagement and dialogue while simultaneously exerting trade restrictions. "The EU cannot expect to gain benefits by imposing restrictions. Unilateral measures run counter to WTO rules, and the consequences will only cut the EU's nose to spite its face. China will not accept such measures," Li Yong, a senior research fellow at the China Association of International Trade, told the Global Times on Tuesday. Li noted that the delegation's visit coincides with Brussels drafting restrictions targeting Chinese chemicals, furniture and machinery alongside new levies on small parcels - a posture that treats trade curbs as bargaining chips to create background pressure on Beijing. As for the visit's prospects, Li said that "the outcome largely depends on whether Europe abandons pressure tactics and meets China halfway. Irrationality of the EU's contradictory stance Bao Jianyun, dean and professor of the Department of International Politics at the School of International Studies at the Renmin University of China, told the Global Times on Tuesday that the EU's contradictory China posture originates from its internal economic woes. "Sharp internal contradictions in Europe - including growth headwinds, trade deficits, employment pressure, and rising politicization of economic issues - are pushing the bloc toward a harder line on China," Bao said. However, seeking to use trade curbs on China as a quick fix for domestic economic troubles stems from flawed logic, the expert stressed. China's Foreign Ministry said earlier that "the root causes of the challenges facing the EU do not lie with China" and called for deeper cooperation. Li pointed out that "Europe may try to secure limited small concessions from China, but this tactic will not work. China boasts robust trade capacity and holds its own leverage. Europe's past leverage is fading; it should drop illusions and engage with China from a realistic footing." Analysts noted that the EU's reported new curbs on Chinese imports would involve a large amount of intermediate products, which could be essential materials that support EU factories. "The EU, including manufacturing power Germany, faces deindustrialization and declining manufacturing competitiveness. Chinese intermediate goods exports can particularly help ease Europe's manufacturing bottlenecks," Li said. According to analytical data, China's intermediate goods exports to the EU account for about half of its total exports to the bloc. This means that Chinese products help reduce the production costs of EU factories, thereby increasing the competitiveness of EU exports. "Cooperation with China is not a 'loss' for Europe - it creates industrial opportunities. The key is whether Europe adopts a realistic, problem-solving approach that addresses mutual concerns," Li stressed. Restrictions on Chinese intermediate goods will raise costs for European manufacturers and consumers, the very people the EU says it is protecting, experts noted. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said on Tuesday that "as far as China is concerned, the relationship with the EU is essentially a partnership, and the economic and trade ties are mutually beneficial," commenting on reports that the EU is planning measures to cut imports of Chinese products from sectors including chemicals, furniture and machinery in the new year. "It is hoped that the EU will abide by the principles of market economy and fair competition, avoid abusing trade remedies, and take concrete actions to promote the steady and sound development of China-EU relations," Guo said. More room for cooperation Despite the contradictory signals from the EU side, analysts welcomed the face-to-face exchanges. "Dialogue itself is valuable, and the space for cooperation is larger than the space for friction. The INTA delegation's trip shows EU's recognition that China-EU trade matters," Bao said. Broad areas for collaboration include new energy, AI, big data and mutual investment. "The delegation's visits to Unitree and BrainCo suggest that robotics, AI and embodied intelligence could similarly become areas of cooperation," Li said. Li stressed that the two economies remain highly complementary. He cited the case of ZXMOTO, a Chinese motorcycle manufacturer, as a model of how bilateral partnership can deliver success. In March 2026, French rider Valentin Debise rode a ZXMOTO bike to a double victory in the WorldSSP category at the Portuguese round of the World Superbike Championship, marking the first win by a Chinese brand. "That is what China-EU cooperation should look like," Li said, emphasizing the combination of Chinese technology and products with European distribution, racing expertise, and professionalism, competing for world titles rather than erecting barriers. China and the EU are fully capable of properly addressing economic and trade differences through open and pragmatic dialogue and consultation. In October 2026, China and the EU reached an arrangement on hybrid vehicle trade. "An upward adjustment from the 2025 baseline was agreed to guarantee Chinese exporters room for steady growth and accommodate industries' legitimate concerns. No measures shall single out Chinese products or discriminate against Chinese firms," a spokesperson for MOFCOM stated on October 12. For electric vehicles, the two sides secured a "soft landing" for the EU's countervailing duty case in January this year, when the EU issued general guidance on price undertakings. MOFCOM also indicated that the consensus safeguards the interests of Chinese enterprises, avoids the escalation of trade friction between China and the EU, and provides a stable, predictable and sustainable trade and investment environment for China and the EU.

item.title: AI boom, high-tech prowess fuel China's industrial profit growth, with momentum set to continue: experts
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27 21:55:00
Vessels are docked at the production base of Dalian Shipbuilding Industry Co, Ltd in Dalian, Northeast China's Liaoning Province, on October 27, 2026. Photo: CNS Photo China's drive to translate technological innovation into economic growth is gaining traction on factory floors and corporate balance sheets, as profits at major industrial firms rose 15.5 percent year-on-year in the first nine months of 2026. This increase was fueled by strong earnings in artificial intelligence (AI)-related industries and high-tech manufacturing, despite global economic uncertainties. Industrial firms with annual main business revenue of at least 20 million yuan ($2.8 million) recorded combined profits of 6.03 trillion yuan from January to September, according to data released by the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) on Tuesday. Profit growth jumped to 14.4 percent year-on-year in September, up from 4.2 percent in August. These gains came as China stepped up efforts to support growth, cultivate new quality productive forces, and upgrade its industrial sector amid persistent global trade and economic uncertainties. Industrial production has remained steady, with cumulative profit growth staying in double digits so far this year, reflecting continued progress in the high-quality development of the industrial economy, Yu Weining, chief statistician of the Industrial Statistics Department of the NBS, said in a statement on Tuesday. Chinese economists noted that the strong earnings indicated a more self-sustaining industrial growth model, as technological advances generate profits that fuel further investment and expansion. They expect the momentum to carry into the fourth quarter, backed by continued innovation, wider industrial applications and potential policy support. From innovation to profits The electronics industry emerged as a key driver of industrial profit growth, as technological iteration and industrial upgrading continued to improve its performance. Profits in the sector doubled year-on-year in the first nine months, contributing 9.6 percentage points to the overall 15.5 percent increase, according to the NBS. Strong demand for AI computing power and advanced memory technologies pushed profits in electronic specialty materials manufacturing up 220 percent, while those in semiconductor discrete device manufacturing rose 51.7 percent. Profits in optoelectronic component and electronic circuit manufacturing both climbed more than 60 percent, driven by the rapid development of next-generation information technology. High-tech manufacturing also posted strong gains, with profits surging 52 percent year-on-year, 36.5 percentage points above the overall industrial growth rate. The sector's share of total industrial profits reached 25.5 percent, up 6.2 percentage points from a year earlier. Meanwhile, expanding computing power and data center construction helped boost profits in optical fiber manufacturing by 570 percent and optical cable manufacturing by 110 percent. Tian Yun, a Beijing-based veteran economist, noted that China's double-digit industrial profit growth was particularly impressive given the sheer scale of its manufacturing sector. He attributed the strong performance increasingly to R&D investment and technological innovation, marking a shift away from the traditional reliance on production scale and cost advantages. "Innovation is spreading beyond industry giants to smaller component manufacturers and advanced materials producers, strengthening China's broader manufacturing ecosystem," Tian told the Global Times on Tuesday. The latest earnings figures signal a profound shift: Emerging industries are developing a more sustainable and market-driven growth model, Hu Qimu, a professor at the Maritime Silk Road Institute of Huaqiao University, told the Global Times. Earlier NBS data showed that investment in high-tech manufacturing rose 4 percent year-on-year in the first three quarters, while the sector's value-added output grew 14.3 percent, well above the 5.3 percent increase in overall industrial production. Hu said the strong profitability is further evidence that these investments and production gains are yielding tangible commercial returns. "The resulting earnings give companies more resources to fund R&D and expand operations, helping create a self-reinforcing cycle of innovation, profitability and reinvestment." New growth drivers are playing an increasingly prominent role in China's industrial expansion. Led by high-tech and digital product manufacturing, they accounted for over 20 percent of value-added output at major industrial firms but contributed more than half of overall industrial growth in the first three quarters, official data showed. Their contribution topped 60 percent in the third quarter alone. Stronger momentum ahead The benefits of emerging industries are spreading beyond high-tech manufacturing, as growing demand for AI and new energy technologies boosts profits in upstream industries. Profits in raw materials manufacturing rose 44.9 percent year-on-year in the first nine months, contributing 5.9 percentage points to overall industrial profit growth, according to the NBS. Strong demand for copper, aluminum, and other base metals from AI and new energy industries pushed profits in the nonferrous metals sector up 79.7 percent. Hu said the impact could extend further, as AI, integrated circuits, and other digital technologies are increasingly adopted across traditional industries, helping manufacturers modernize production, improve efficiency and unlock new growth opportunities. China's latest policy push also seeks to extend the benefits of innovation across traditional industries. Guidelines released on October 21 by the general offices of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and the State Council called for closer integration of technological and industrial innovation, faster commercialization of research breakthroughs and the use of advanced technologies to upgrade traditional manufacturing. Meanwhile, China's sustained investment in R&D and technological innovation is helping manufacturers close gaps in domestic supply chains, develop higher-value products and strengthen their global competitiveness, while expanding the supply of advanced products to international markets, according to Tian. According to customs data, China's exports of integrated circuits surged 99.1 percent year-on-year in the first nine months, while electric vehicle exports rose 72.3 percent, lithium-ion battery exports increased 36.4 percent, and exports of wind turbines and their components grew 22.4 percent. Looking ahead, the NBS said on Tuesday that China will expand domestic demand, improve supply, and accelerate the shift toward new growth drivers to strengthen the economy's internal momentum and advance high-quality industrial development. The policy direction follows a State Council executive meeting on September 28, which called for stronger countercyclical adjustments and measures to promote effective investment, aiming to address challenges in economic operations and achieve the country's annual development targets. Experts expect China's industrial economy to maintain its growth momentum in the fourth quarter, supported by relatively stable external demand, continued expansion in emerging industries and the prospect of additional policy measures. "High-tech manufacturing, integrated circuits, AI and related software and services are likely to sustain relatively rapid growth as markets expand and new applications emerge," Hu said, noting that these sectors have shown some resilience to traditional economic cycles. Tian said stronger domestic demand will unlock further gains. With China's manufacturing competitiveness and innovation capabilities continuing to improve, stronger demand will help translate more technological advances into market opportunities and corporate profits, he added.

item.title: Mbappé apologizes for inappropriate remarks in French, Chinese and English after strong backlash in China
item.description:

French football player Kylian Mbappé has apologized for his extremely inappropriate remarks that have drawn anger and fierce criticism in China. French football player Kylian Mbappé has apologized for his extremely inappropriate remarks that have drawn anger and fierce criticism in China. In a statement issued on Tuesday and published in French, Chinese and English, he said his comment was "ill-judged" and that "I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world." "I have deep respect for the Chinese people and their history, and I am sincerely sorry," he said in the statement. item.title: Chinese-led research team identifies fastest-rotating near-Earth asteroid, advancing early-warning capabilities
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27 19:35:00
A screenshot from an animation of a Chinese asteroid defense mission Photo: VCG A Chinese-led international research team has identified the fastest-rotating near-Earth asteroid known to date and improved methods for determining the physical characteristics of asteroids that require short-term early warning. The findings mark a breakthrough in the observation and study of rapidly rotating near-Earth asteroids and are expected to enhance capabilities for advanced monitoring, early warning and defense against asteroid threats that allow little time for response, the Global Times learned from the research team on Tuesday. The research team, led by Zhang Xiliang, a researcher at the Yunnan Observatories, Chinese Academy of Sciences, and Fan Xiangyu, a doctoral student at the Yunnan Observatories, working with domestic and international collaborators, has published its findings in the international journal The Astronomical Journal. Near-Earth asteroids (NEAs) are asteroids with heliocentric distances less than 1.3 au. Those larger than 140 meters and having a minimum orbit intersection distance with Earth of less than 0.05 au are designated as potentially hazardous asteroids (PHAs). The destructive potential of near-Earth asteroid impacts has attracted growing public attention and concern, making monitoring, early warning and planetary defense against near-Earth asteroids essential to protect humanity. As of October 10, 2026, about 42,752 near-Earth asteroids had been confirmed, including 2,542 potentially hazardous asteroids, according to the Minor Planet Center of International Astronomical Union. The small size, faintness and high speed of these asteroids make their early detection and accurate assessment of their impact energy extremely challenging. In all the 13 cases to date in which humanity has successfully predicted near-Earth asteroid impacts, the asteroids were meter-sized, and the warning times ranged from two to 21 hours. Near-Earth asteroid 2024 XA1 entered Earth's atmosphere over eastern Siberia in the early hours of December 4, 2024, Beijing time, just 10 hours after its discovery, marking humanity's 11th successful prediction of an asteroid impact. 2.4-meter Lijiang Telescope Photo: Courtesty of Zhang Xiliang To efficiently obtain brightness data for asteroid 2024 XA1, the research team used the 2.4-meter Lijiang Telescope to capture images of asteroid 2024 XA1 during the final hour before it entered Earth's atmosphere. The research results show that near-Earth asteroid 2024 XA1 has a rotation period of just 1.63 seconds, surpassing the previous record of 2.58 seconds held by asteroid 2024 BX1 to become the fastest-rotating near-Earth asteroid known to date. The asteroid's extreme rotation generates centrifugal acceleration far exceeding its gravitational acceleration, indicating that it is a solid, strength-dominated monolithic body rather than a loosely gravitationally bound rubble pile. It may have formed through the collision and fragmentation of a larger celestial body. The study not only confirmed 2024 XA1 as the fastest-rotating near-Earth asteroid known to date but also offered new insights into the internal structure of rapidly rotating, fast-moving meter-scale asteroids and enhanced the ability to characterize short-term warning asteroids.

item.title: With extremely inappropriate remarks, Mbappé loses trust in the Chinese market on his own
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27 16:30:00
Kylian Mbappé Photo: VCG A football star can make hundreds of millions on the pitch, only to lose the trust of an entire market by failing to show the most basic respect. French football star Kylian Mbappé has recently sparked a fierce backlash in China after making extremely inappropriate remarks in a recent interview. What did he say? Many Chinese would rather not repeat it. Dongqiudi, a major Chinese football news and community platform, issued a statement saying that it would not translate the interview because the footballer's remarks had hurt the feelings of Chinese fans and the Chinese people. Brands including Dongpeng Beverage Group and Chinese dairy giant Mengniu promptly terminated their cooperation. This is not an emotional outburst, but a rational choice made spontaneously by the market. The message from Chinese consumers is clear: Respect is not optional; one doesn't get to profit from China while disrespecting it. Not a chance. Mbappé's talent and skills are beyond doubt. But talent and public responsibility are two entirely different things. The first determines how many goals you score and how much you are worth; the second determines how many people are still willing to pay for you. Talent may open the door to a market, but respect is what keeps it open. We don't know whether Mbappé would deliberately set out to offend a country whose market has helped fuel his commercial success. One thing is for sure: He lacks cross-cultural awareness, and fails to appreciate the responsibilities that come with global fame. Had he shown even a basic understanding of Chinese culture and sensitivities, he might have thought twice before speaking so disrespectfully. Every culture has its boundaries. That is no secret. No one expects a foreign athlete to be an expert on China. But global superstars who have long profited from commercial partnerships in China should make an effort to understand the country's cultural sensitivities and show a basic level of respect. That is not asking for special treatment. It is basic commercial common sense. For Chinese brands, terminating such cooperation is no small decision. Previous marketing investments, contractual obligations and the cost of replacing promotional materials all mean real costs. Yet, by cutting ties, these companies are sending a clear message: When public sentiment is offended, businesses cannot pretend nothing has happened. China's market remains open and welcomes athletes and brands from around the world to share in its opportunities. But an open market is not a market without boundaries. The threshold is respect. Those who disregard the feelings of the Chinese people should not expect to escape the commercial consequences. For decades, some international public figures have been happy to take the money from the Chinese market while talking carelessly about China. When it comes to matters of principle, they tend to dismiss offensive remarks as "personal expression" or hide behind "freedom of speech." That's no excuse. This time, Mbappé has learned the hard way — and he has only himself to blame. His case should serve as a clear red line for every foreign public figure hoping to profit from China: On issues of national sentiment, no one has the freedom to act recklessly. Going forward, our commercial contracts might as well spell out clearer clauses governing public conduct. The national feelings of the Chinese people are not to be provoked, and the Chinese market will leave no room for those who display arrogance and disrespect.

item.title: China's upgraded Jiaolong submersible completes 7,000-meter-class sea trials
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27 16:11:00
China's upgraded manned deep-sea submersible Jiaolong is recovered on October 2, 2026, after completing its 465th dive, during which it reached a depth of 7,056.9 meters. Photo: Xinhua China's upgraded manned deep-sea submersible Jiaolong has successfully completed multiple 7,000-meter-class sea trials in the Philippine Basin, confirming the reliability and safety of the upgraded submersible and its domestically produced key components and strengthening China's technological edge in manned deep-sea exploration equipment, the Xinhua News Agency reported on Tuesday. The sea trials were conducted as part of the second leg of China's 100th oceanographic expedition. The submersible completed three test dives in the Philippine Basin, including two dives to depths exceeding 7,000 meters, reaching a maximum depth of 7,056.9 meters. All test parameters met the requirements for 7,000-meter-class sea trials. Sun Yongfu, a researcher at the National Deep Sea Center, said the sea trials fully verified the reliability and safety of Jiaolong following its iterative upgrades and the replacement of key components with domestically produced alternatives, consolidating and enhancing China's technological advantages in manned deep-sea submersible technology. Before the scientific expedition, the submersible received major upgrades, including a 7,000-meter-class high-energy-density lithium battery pack, domestically developed low-noise DC thrusters and advanced hydraulic and imaging systems. The upgrades introduced technological innovations across key components and systems, including power supply, propulsion, hydraulics, electrical systems, and communication and observation, significantly enhancing the submersible's operational capabilities. According to Sun, following its upgrades and the localization of key components, the submersible conducted multiple scientific missions in different sea areas to investigate deep-sea resources and marine ecosystems. These scientific expeditions will further deepen international cooperation in marine science, significantly advancing China's deep-sea exploration and research, and contribute to the country's goal of becoming a maritime power, Sun said. item.title: Why has the CPC succeeded? The fifth plenary session provides a window of observation: Global Times editorial
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27 00:51:00
The view of Beijing's Central Business District Photo: VCG How has this massive party of unprecedented scale demonstrated formidable organizational mobilization and implementation capacity when confronted with major risks and challenges? When the international community turns its attention to the fifth plenary session, it is not just observing China's politics; more importantly, it seeks insights from "China's governance" for political party building, national governance across the world, and even the reform of the global governance system. The 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC) is holding its fifth plenary session in Beijing from October 26 to 29 to deliberate on major issues concerning the continued advancement of full and rigorous Party self-governance. Marking the 105th anniversary of the founding of the CPC and the launch year of the 15th Five-Year Plan, this plenary session draws global attention to the underlying foundations of China's development. Particularly against the backdrop of partisan politics in many countries being mired in polarized, fragmented and chaotic contests, with many ruling parties feeling helpless in the face of social division and stalled development at home, why does China present a completely different picture? The fifth plenary session serves as an important window for the world to gain insights. For anyone following China, today's China is defined not merely by economic growth, technological breakthroughs and landmark projects. The robust organizational capacity and political strength underpinning these remarkable achievements further illuminate the source of China's steady progress amid profound changes of the times. As the largest governing party in the world, the CPC maintains solidarity and unity at all times. How has this massive party of unprecedented scale demonstrated formidable organizational mobilization and implementation capacity when confronted with major risks and challenges? When the international community turns its attention to the fifth plenary session, it is not just observing China's politics; more importantly, it seeks insights from "China's governance" for political party building, national governance across the world, and even the reform of the global governance system. An increasing number of insightful observers around the world have identified a clear thread running through China's development: The leadership of the CPC has consistently served as the central pillar underpinning the steady advancement of the country's various undertakings and is the master key to unlocking the secret behind the success of "the governance of China." Persistently advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance constitutes the fundamental mechanism at the heart of this master key. Since the 18th CPC National Congress, the great new project of Party building in the new era has been advanced in depth. China has continuously intensified its fight against corruption, improved its intra-Party oversight system, and made sustained efforts to enhance Party conduct through regular and long-term mechanisms. These efforts have included combating formalism and bureaucratism, holding officials accountable for dereliction of duty and failure to fulfill their responsibilities, and encouraging officials to take initiative and fulfill their duties. Such measures have helped ensure that decisions and plans made by the central leadership are effectively implemented at all levels and that resources and efforts from across society remain consistently directed toward shared goals. This political courage to turn the blade inward and confront problems within the Party itself is rarely seen in the history of political parties worldwide. For a long time, many voices in international public discourse have taken it for granted that there are only a handful of established models for building a governing party, as though effective governance could be achieved only by replicating certain institutional frameworks. China has challenged these conventional assumptions with verifiable development data. One of the most tangible outcomes of these measures is that public trust in the ruling party in China has remained consistently high for many years. Meanwhile, the efficiency with which major national strategies are implemented and the continuity of public policy execution have gained widespread international recognition. The principle that the governance over the Party must precede the governance of the country is grounded in concrete and profound practical realities. In today's international community, a stark contrast has emerged between "China's governance" and "the West's chaos." Some Western countries that firmly believe in multiparty systems and the separation of powers are mired in intensified partisan conflicts and frequent changes of government. Internal political polarization is escalating, societal divisions are deepening, and public policies fluctuate under the tug-of-war of interest groups, making it difficult to reach consensus even on basic livelihood issues. Some Western scholars, after comparing the party politics of major powers, have had to admit that "the CPC possesses strong governing capacity." In recent years, party representatives from various regions, including Southeast Asia, Africa, Europe, and Latin America, have come to China to study and learn from the governance experiences of the CPC through inter-party exchanges. China's long-term approach to development, strategic vision, and practical achievements have opened up broader intellectual space for countries to independently explore political development paths that align with their own national conditions. The world today needs truly effective governance solutions more than ever. An increasing number of countries and political parties are drawing inspiration from "China's governance" to explore governance paths that suit their own national situations. This not only provides more diverse practical solutions for the global governance system but also strengthens the consensus among countries to collectively address global challenges. It is also the precious public value contributed by China through its unwavering efforts to promote full and rigorous Party self-governance amid a world marked by intertwined changes and turmoil.

item.title: GT Voice: Rare-earth metal recycling should not be driven by geopolitics
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-26 22:05:00
Rare earth File photo:VCG An American recycling company is recovering rare-earth metals from old wind turbines, which The Wall Street Journal said over the weekend could be one part of a drive to help reduce US reliance on China for the materials. While recycling critical materials from retired equipment can tap existing resources, treating rare-earth magnet recycling as a breakthrough to achieve critical minerals "self-sufficiency" or framing it as a shortcut to shake off reliance on China's supply chain, seriously underestimates industrial realities. Rare-earth metals are widely used in wind power systems, new-energy vehicles and high-end manufacturing, serving as core components of the modern industrial system. As these industries expand, recycling materials from old equipment has broad long-term potential. But being technically recoverable is not the same as being commercially viable and capable of stable industrial supply. The disassembly, separation and purification of wind turbines involve highly complex processes, which place high demands on specialized equipment, technical expertise and environmental protection treatment. Once transportation, labor and processing costs are added up, whether recycled products can compete with existing supplies on price and quality still has to be tested by the market. An even trickier hurdle lies in the stability of the feedstock. Wind turbines are generally engineered for service lives of more than two decades. Most large-scale wind farms installed across Europe and the US came online only in the past decade, so very few turbines have reached retirement age. Even if some turbines are replaced with better models, recyclers may still face uneven, scattered and non-standardized feedstock. Without reliable raw material inflows, downstream separation and refining lines cannot run at full capacity, economies of scale remain out of reach, and unit costs stay high. This means recycling can serve as a valuable supplement to critical mineral supplies, but it cannot replace mature supply chains any time soon. In recent years, some Western countries have repeatedly discussed critical mineral security and rolled out multiple policy initiatives, but actual progress has been relatively limited. The problem is not a lack of political will but the fact that building industrial chains follows its own logic. The global supply of critical minerals is never an isolated contest over a single link or a single technology. It is a systemic ecosystem integrating resources, technical expertise, cost control, skilled talent, specialized equipment and downstream market support. Mine development involves long investment cycles, separation and purification pose high technical barriers, and downstream manufacturing requires decades of accumulated experience. A shortfall in any single link will drag down the entire industrial chain. Recycling and refining are never simple matters of technological breakthroughs. The chain equally requires a complete process system, stable raw material supply and a sustainable business model, all of which are necessary. Treating recycling as a shortcut to bypass existing mature supply chains underestimates the systemic difficulty of industrial chain construction. China's rare-earth industry took shape over decades of steady accumulation. Yet today, some economies enjoy the benefits of the global division of labor while framing normal supply relationships as risks and seeking to sever industrial chains. Meanwhile, there is no such thing as a shortcut in the global critical mineral industrial chain. The formation of a mature industrial system is the long-term combined result of resource endowment, technology accumulation, market scale and cost structure. It cannot be completely rearranged by a few technological breakthroughs or several policy measures. China's rare-earth export measures are fully reasonable and compliant and have long provided stable, reliable supplies for related industries across the world. By hyping "reducing dependence on China," some economies appear to be pursuing supply chain security; in reality they are narrowing their own path of development. Supply chain security can never be achieved through artificial fragmentation. Overall, recycling rare-earth metals from old wind turbines is a worthwhile pursuit within the circular economy, but it should be judged as a supplementary industrial strategy - not burdened with geopolitical expectations.
